title: Who finances Hawaii home purchases, by county and price tier (HMDA 2025 vs 2019)

source.publisher: FFIEC / CFPB HMDA Data Browser API, public loan-level LAR (modified LAR fields)
source.latest_year: 2025 is the latest HMDA activity year available (a 2026 request returned HTTP 400; see an/new/hmda.json). 2025 = loans originated in calendar 2025.

method: Universe: action_taken=1 (originated), loan_purpose=1 (home purchase), lien_status=1 (first lien), total_units in {1,2,3,4}, construction_method=1 (site-built; drops 1 manufactured-home loan each year, consistent with an/new/hmda.json), county_code in 15001/15003/15007/15009. Filter funnel per year in 'funnel'. Final n: 2025 = 9,707; 2019 = 13,312.
Unit = one first-lien purchase loan, i.e. one mortgage-financed purchase. Piggyback seconds are excluded by the first-lien filter.

Tier assigned from property_value: entry < $750K; mid $750K to < $1.5M; upper $1.5M to < $3M; luxury $3M to < $10M; ultra >= $10M. HMDA publishes property_value as the midpoint of the $10,000 interval containing the true value (e.g. 745000 = $740,000-$749,999). Every numeric value in both files ends in 5000, and all tier cut-offs are multiples of $10K, so each bin falls wholly inside one tier and the tier assignment is exact. Records with property_value NA or Exempt are kept in a separate 'unknown' tier (2025: 133; 2019: 202).

Occupancy mix from occupancy_type (1 principal residence, 2 second residence, 3 investment property). Loan type mix from loan_type (1 conventional, 2 FHA, 3 VA, 4 USDA/RHS-FSA). Shares are over all loans in the cell.

Median applicant income = median of the HMDA 'income' field (gross annual income relied on in the credit decision, applicant plus any co-applicant, in thousands of USD), NA excluded; n reported and n NA reported. Quantiles use linear interpolation (Excel PERCENTILE.INC).

Age mix from applicant_age (primary applicant's age band). 8888 = not a natural person (entity borrower) is shown as its own band; shares are given over all loans and over natural persons only. Summary shares under-35 (<25 + 25-34) and 55-plus (55-64 + 65-74 + >74) are over natural persons.

Jumbo = conforming_loan_limit flag 'NC' (loan amount above the FHFA conforming limit for that county and year). Given over all loans and over conventional loans only; the conventional share is the true 'jumbo product' share, because NC on a VA/FHA loan just means a large government loan.
Extra context fields per cell (not requested, labeled as such): business_or_commercial_purpose share, median combined loan-to-value and share with CLTV <= 60, median property value.

VA (military/veteran buyers): loan_type=3 within the same universe, by county and year: count, share of county loans, median and quartiles of property value, median income, occupancy and tier distribution, and VA share of each tier.
Small cells: every cell carries small_cell_flag_n_lt_20 = true when n < 20. Do not quote percentages from flagged cells as rates.
notes: HMDA covers mortgage-financed purchases only. Cash purchases are absent, so the upper, luxury and ultra tiers show only the financed minority of buyers. Use the conveyance/sales data for total counts; this file describes who borrows.
HMDA does not separate condos from single-family houses: both fall under 'Single Family (1-4 Units):Site-Built'. A house vs condo split is not possible from this source.
Geography is county only in this file. Census tract is in the raw data, but no district or ZIP split was made here.

Second-home vs investment coding shifted between 2019 and 2025 (see an/new/hmda.json notes; GSE second-home pricing changes and more DSCR/business-purpose investor lending are plausible but untested causes). For trends, prefer the combined non-owner-occupied share.

Jumbo shares are not like-for-like across years. The conforming limit rose much more between 2019 and 2025 than many loan sizes did, which explains why the mid-tier conventional jumbo share fell from 28% to under 1%.

Ultra tier (>= $10M): 6 loans statewide in 2025 (Hawaii County 3, Honolulu 3) and 4 in 2019 (Hawaii County 2, Maui 2). Every ultra cell is flagged small and is reported for completeness only. Other small cells: 2019 luxury in Hawaii County (n=10) and Kauai (n=14), plus some 'unknown' property-value cells. 2025 county luxury cells clear the threshold but only just (Hawaii County 23, Kauai 22, Maui 32, Honolulu 73), so their mix percentages move by 4-5 points per loan.
Maui County 2025 volume reflects the post-August-2023 Lahaina wildfire market as well as interest rates; HMDA cannot separate these effects.
Income NA is more common for investor and entity loans (DSCR-style underwriting), so median income in investor-heavy cells describes only the borrowers whose income was used.

Race, ethnicity and sex fields were not read into any statistic or output. Only these fields were used: county_code, action_taken, loan_purpose, lien_status, total_units, construction_method, property_value, occupancy_type, loan_type, income, applicant_age, conforming_loan_limit, loan_to_value_ratio, business_or_commercial_purpose.
No owner names, addresses, parcel ids or loan-level records are output; all values are cell aggregates.
Edition: the 2025 data match the 2025 Snapshot. For 2019 the API does not say which edition it serves (snapshot, one-year or three-year), so counts may differ slightly from a specific static file.
